headline: Approved 2027 meeting schedule, recommended written reports to Legislative Council every two months, and discussed a Whitney Center partnership.
summary: Members discussed vacancies, Veterans Awareness Day planning, a possible Hamden Veterans Coalition, and a possible Whitney Center partnership. They approved the corrected September minutes and the 2027 meeting dates.
decisions: Approved the corrected September meeting minutes unanimously.
Approved the 2027 meeting dates, held on the first Wednesday of each month at 5:30 PM.
Recommended submitting written reports to the Legislative Council every two months.
Agreed to update the office coverage schedule and send it to all members.

decision_titles: Submitting reports to the Legislative Council every two months
plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Veterans Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
5:30 PM, October 7, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 Chair Bill Macmullen called the meeting to order at 5:30 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 Present:  
Chair: Bill Macmullen 
Porsche Edmundson, Boards and Commissions Clerk. 
Commissioners: Dave Lewis, Mike Doyle, Cal Shepard, Tyrone Mitchell, Barry Elliott, and 
Jim O'Neil. 
Absent: Commissioners Reggie Mayberry, Bill Compton, and Johnnie Best. 
A quorum was present. 
3. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE   
 The Commission recited the Pledge of Allegiance. 
4. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 The Commission reviewed the September meeting minutes and corrected the Veterans 
Awareness Day event date to November 5, 2026. 
The Commission made a motion to approve the corrected minutes, which was seconded 
and approved unanimously. 
5. PUBLIC COMMENT / INTRODUCTION OF GUESTS   
 New Commissioner Tyrone Mitchell was introduced and welcomed. We appreciate his 
continued interest, dedication, and willingness to serve the Hamden Community. 
 No public comments were received. 
6. CORRESPONDENCE   
 Commissioner Dave Lewis reported on a Knights of Columbus-sponsored veterans' visit to 
the New England Air Museum. The Commission discussed organizing a future visit or 
collaborating with other veterans' organizations on educational outings. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION   
 No Executive Session was held. 
8. REPORTS   
 Community Relations: No formal report was presented.
Student Member Recruitment:  
The Commission discussed filling the student representative vacancy after Owen Arenberg 
left due to age eligibility. Members will explore recruitment through administrators at 
Hamden High School.. 
 
Wreaths Across America: 
Mike Doyle agreed to assist with wreath-related activities moving forward. Chairman 
Macmullen reported discussions with a local Hamden dentist of Korean heritage who 
expressed an interest in supporting veterans' initiatives and participating in future Veterans 
Day activities. Members discussed developing a more formal process for community 
members to sponsor wreaths and get involved in Commission events. 
9. OLD BUSINESS   
 There was no Old Business requiring action. 
10. NEW BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Announcements.  
  Legislative Council Meeting and Commission Vacancies. 
 
Chair Macmullen reported on a recent appearance before the Legislative Council 
regarding vacancies on the Veterans Affairs Commission. Commission 
representatives expressed concerns about delays in appointments and the impact 
these vacancies have on the Commission’s ability to function effectively. 
 
The Chair also reported learning that commissions may submit periodic written 
reports to the Legislative Council. It was recommended that the Veterans Affairs 
Commission begin submitting reports every two months to provide updates on 
activities, initiatives, and needs. 
The Commission further discussed communication issues involving appointments and 
notifications from various municipal offices. Members welcomed the addition of 
Tyrone Mitchell and discussed efforts to fill remaining vacancies. 
 
Commission Leadership and Term Planning 
Chair Macmullen discussed long-term leadership planning and the importance of 
mentoring future Commission leaders. Members also discussed health concerns 
currently affecting Commissioner Reggie Mayberry, who was unable to attend the 
meeting. 
 
Veterans Awareness Day Planning; 
An extensive review was conducted regarding planning for Veterans Awareness Day. 
Commission members reviewed participant lists, organizational contacts, display 
requests, and event logistics. Updates were provided regarding numerous 
organizations, agencies, veteran service groups, military associations, educational 
institutions, historical organizations, and community partners that have either 
confirmed participation or are being contacted. 
Members noted that planning efforts are entering the final stages and emphasized the 
importance of obtaining final participation confirmations before the next meeting.
2. HAC Welcome and protocol manual, Cal Shepard.  
  The Commission discussed updates to the Commission’s protocol manual and 
operating procedures. 
 
  
  3. Office Manning Schedule — W. MacMullen.  
  Members reviewed the office coverage schedule maintained by the Commission 
Office.  
A concern was raised regarding a resident who had reportedly visited during 
scheduled office hours and was unable to connect with the Commissioner.  
The Commission agreed to update the schedule to remove individuals no longer 
serving and distribute the schedule to all members. 
  
  4. HVC reached out to Whitney Center Veterans — Cal Shepard.  
  Whitney Center Collaboration 
Cal Shepard reported on ongoing discussions with representatives from Whitney 
Center regarding future collaborations. The Commission discussed potential 
opportunities to: 
• Hold meetings at Whitney Center; 
• Increase participation among resident veterans; 
• Develop educational programming; and 
• Partner on Veterans Day and Memorial Day activities. 
Members expressed support for hosting a future Commission meeting at Whitney 
Center. 
 
  
  5. Term limits.  
  Commission Leadership and Term Planning 
Chair Macmullen discussed long-term leadership planning and the importance of 
mentoring future Commission leaders. Members also discussed health concerns 
currently affecting Commissioner Reggie Mayberry, who was unable to attend the 
meeting. 
 
 
 
  
  6. Hamden Veterans Coalition.  
  The Commission discussed the concept of a Hamden Veterans Coalition that would 
allow veterans who cannot serve on the Commission due to residency or appointment 
limitations to participate in discussions and activities. While coalition members would 
not have voting authority, they could support Commission initiatives and participate in 
events and planning efforts. 
  7. Collaboration with Human Rights.  
  The Commission discussed possible future collaborations with the Hamden Human 
Rights Commission and community partners.
8. Approved 2027 annual meeting dates: the first Wednesday of every month at 5:30 
PM. 
January 6th, February 3rd, March 3rd, April 7th, May 5th, June 2nd, July 7, August 
4th, September 1st, October 6th, November 3rd, December 1st.  
  2027 Annual Meeting Dates 
The Commission reviewed the proposed meeting schedule for the upcoming year. 
The first Wednesday of each month at 5:30 PM remains the preferred meeting time. 
Members discussed flexibility regarding meeting locations and agreed that future 
meetings could be held at community locations when appropriate, provided proper 
notice is given. 
 
  
11. ADJOURNMENT   
 There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made, seconded by Dave Lewis, 
and approved unanimously. 
The meeting adjourned at approximately 6:55 PM. 
 Meeting minutes submitted by: B&C Porsche Edmudnson 
Hamden Veterans Affairs Commission Regular Meeting Minutes October 7, 2026
